newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Alenia test flies Eurofighter prototype.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Alenia test flies Eurofighter prototype.

text.p: An Italian prototype of the Eurofighter 2000 successfully completed its maiden test flight on Monday as part of the jet fighter's four-nation development programme, Italian manufacturer Aleniasaid.
The company, a unit of state-controlled Finmeccanica, said the plane, designated DA7, flew for 35 minutes from Caselle airport outside the northwest city of Turin.
"It is easy to fly and very manoeuvrable," Alenia's statement quoted test pilot Napoleone Bragagnolo as saying.
The partners in the Eurofighter consortium are British Aerospace Plc, Germany's Daimler Benz Aerospace, Alenia and Spain's Casa.
Alenia said DA7 was the fifth of seven prototypes being built as part of the project. The other Italian prototype, DA3, began flying in June 1995.

Alenia said the DA7 would contribute to the development of navigation and communications systems and weapons system integration. The prototype will be flown by air force pilots of the four partner countries in April, it added.

Representatives of the four nations involved in the Eurofighter programme last month reaffirmed their commitment to moving to production of the combat aircraft early this year, but gave no new details on timing.
The key outstanding decision is to be made in Germany, where parliament has to vote on whether to go ahead with purchase.
Germany hopes to order 180 Eurofighters. Britain wants 232 planes from the project, Italy is slated to take 140 and Spain 87.
